2026.title: 2026 Season
2026.blurb: Five weeks in. The 30% check-in is up, and the draft takes are on the table.

posts.title: 2026 Post Draft Rankings
blocks:
Welcome back to the newest installment of "Why Do I Pay Trevor Twenty-Five Dollars a Year Only to Stare at My Phone and Wonder What the Hell I Was Doing When I Drafted All These Dumbass Players." Well, I’m here to answer that, this is the year one of you walks away with two hundred dollars....maybe. Looking at these rankings and where things sit right now, I don’t believe it’s gonna be me unless there’s some miracle of God, and by miracle of God, I mean cheating. Your glorious commissioner, fleecing and finessing every last one of you, taking your best players for the low like this league is a yard sale and I’m the only one who showed up with cash.

I meant to have this out post-draft but life happens and I'm delayed, sue me or dont't read these. That's probably just as hurtful. So with that being said, these are the rankings I had y’all at the second the draft ended, before anybody played a snap. I’m just late, and I didn’t take these first couple weeks into account, so you might be sitting lower than you actually deserve, or you might be floating higher than you have any right to be. Too bad, this is my holy Bible, and it’s what all of you are gonna live by, because these rankings are the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. If y’all can’t handle the truth, then y’all ain’t a few good men.
12. Newpdogg (Olivia)

Holy fucking shit, this team is dick and balls. I couldn’t help but notice while you were drafting that you picked every single Philadelphia Eagle, and yeah they’re a good football team, but when they have a bad week, this whole roster has a bad week. Individually, Jalen, Saquon, Devonta, and Dallas Goedert are great. As a whole-ass fantasy team, boy oh boy are you in trouble.

Jalen throws hella picks, and nowhere close to enough yards for Devonta to be a top tier receiver. Saquon is a beast and a freak of nature, but the way they utilize him is more useless than birth control at Comic-Con. Thank God you have Bo Nix to back you up, oh wait, he’s just as bad. I’ll give him a little grace since he’s coming off an injury, but he still sucks. You don’t really have a running back two either, because the Patriots refuse to use one of the best players on their team. Henderson is a great add, but he’s not gonna have any use until the middle to later half of the season, when they finally get rid of Rhamondre and his butterfingers.

I do like the rest of your team though. CeeDee is an absolute demon. Wait, what’s his name? Did you say CeeDee? See Deez nuts in your face, ooooooo get fucked nerd. And then Stefon Diggs has been a great addition, I thought he might have a bit of a fall off since he's older and Washington already has a WR1 but boy has Diggs been looking good through 2 week. Wait, Diggs? Did you say Diggs? Dicks in your ass, damnnnnnnn, what a double whammy, can’t believe you fell for that twice. In all seriousness, the rest of this team is actually pretty okay. I think you might be able to move up the rankings. At the very beginning of the year I had very little hope for this squad, and it’s still not my favorite, but I’m sure your Uncle Dan will come in and save the day. Hopefully he is nicer than my Uncle Dan who got only ever got me lube and bananas for Christmas. Still don't fully understand that one, but that's neither here nor there. Good luck out there Swoleger!
11. Blowin' My J's (Jordan)

Honestly, for a team that got drafted solely off first names, this squad didn’t turn out bad. You’re surely not first, but at least you’re not last. It might have been a reach to take Josh Allen early, but he is still, arguably definitely, the best fantasy QB in the league. Your other bright spots are obviously Justin Jefferson and Jaylen Waddle, but the problem is they both have terrorists at quarterback. Jefferson is already on his second-string quarterback in week two, and Waddle just has a bum in the backfield. Things might get better, but I fear those two being your best players is a bit troublesome. You better hope Josh Allen keeps dropping forty-bombs more often than Israel is dropping bombs on Gaza.

I honestly don’t hate the running back situation, being a Steeler fan, Jaylen Warren is always an absolute dawg. The problem is they don’t score more than ten points a game, so realistically, what’s his worth? And while Jadarian Price was a first-round pick and there were high hopes for him, I forgot that he plays for the Seahawks, and they never want to utilize their best running back. They’d rather give it to some bum-ass broke boy from Brooklyn and let him get all the end zone work and all the fantasy points. It’s a busted system, almost as bad as well fair am I right? Price works so hard to get to the goal line only to have this good for nothing foreigner (second string) take his lunch money and get a touchdown. God Price worked so hard for that TD and instead the guy who contributed nothing to the drive got the glory, you hate to see it. Imagine if they knew how to use their workhorse running back, maybe then they’d win a Super Bowl or something...oh, wait.

I honestly don’t hate the bench either. The only problem is half of them are already injured and won’t be back for three or four weeks. Brooks, Tyson, and Tongs are all great players, but I fear they won’t be relevant anytime soon. You’ve got one extra spot on your bench, so I would recommend adding a player, perhaps this guy named Jeff Epps. He fits the bill for the team and he's a REALLY good tight end. However, he's also really good at blowing J's which might be staling your thunder but he specializes in the ones under eighteen. Being that you have to be over 18 to play in the NFL, I think you should be in the clear. Stay tuned to see how my attitude changes toward this team over the next few weeks, but realistically I don’t see you moving a whole lot. I’d say try to work some trades, but I fear you already have all the best players with the letter J in their name, so not many opportunities are likely to present themselves. May Jesus jerk your jubilee junkies and turn this into a winning team. Good luck out there, kid.
10. Jockstraps (Haley)

God damn, bitch, what were you thinking when you made this team? I mean, you have two of the best wide receivers in the league. JSN is popping more pussy than Iggy Azalea in 2016, and Parker Washington is looking like the true breakout in Jacksonville. He’s zesty as hell, and give Karl Anthony Towns a run for his money, but if that boy can get a touchdown, who cares? I even like having Drake London on the bench, even though he’s on the most dogshit offense in the league. And let me tell you, Atlanta knows a thing or two about dog shit, just ask Michael Vick, he is very familiar with dogs and the shit that comes with them.  Speaking of quarterbacks whose name is Michael and their last name is one letter away from being a synonym for a dick, Michael Penix being back this upcoming week will likely skyrocket his value. Granted, it’s already in the hell, so it’s not like it can really go down from here.

The problem I see with this team is the running backs. Montgomery had a great week one, but the Texans are going to revert back to their old ways, and C.J. Stroud is gonna continue to suck more dick than Tiana Trump (no relation), if you don’t know who that is, I suggest you look it up, that woman works wonders. So while Monty had a great first week, I fear that’s the outlier, and they’re going to keep working in Woody Marks and cut into his value and his share. Breece Hall is a phenomenal player too, however, he is tied to a bottom-ten team, and if we’re being honest, it’s probably a bottom-five team, despite them somehow being 1-1, I don’t expect this to continue, and I don’t think the Jets will often be playing from behind where they'll have to air it out and he may go hungry.

You do have the reigning MVP on your team in Matt Stafford, but two weeks into the season this man is looking like he went to the woods with Aaron Rodgers to do some ayahuasca. Week one he took a big old dookie in his pants, but week two he showed up against an atrocious New York defense. Granted, he’s gone two weeks without his best receiver in Puka, so maybe things will turn around. Don’t put too much faith in that though because Puka is on the Antonio Brown track trying to become CTE 2.0. I know I got you kinda low in the rankings, but I think this team could for sure move up. To be fair, there aren’t many places for you to go down, seeing that Olivia who can only name Eagles players is the bottom and Jordan who picked his team solely based off the letter of the player’s name is one up on her. So while it’s not the best team, it certainly is not the worst, and I think this squad could for sure make some moves up my rankings here in a few weeks.
9. Baby Choda (Brendan)

Well, well, well if it isn’t the king of the chodes himself. Looking at this team now, a couple weeks into the schedule, I do believe you probably should be higher. Alas, I’m here to make fun of you, because this was my read on the squad before the season started. So let’s dive in. First of all, this is your first year without your glorious king, Josh Allen. I know it must be tough to have him ripped from your soft, voluptuous, manly, strokable hands. Instead you landed Patrick Mahomes in one of the late rounds, and boy oh boy has he looked good. He’s reverted back to his old habits of sounding like Kermit the Frog and putting his name in the hat for MVP.

Despite that, you have two super solid running backs in JT and De’Von Achane. Obviously JT is one of the best in the league, and Achane is extremely explosive. The only problem is he’s on the Dolphins, who are one of the least explosive teams in the league, and Malik Willis is absolutely useless at throwing checkdowns to his running backs. Interesting that you would pick some guy so explosive as soon as I move out of the house, you must really be missing me, trying to find someone or something to fill the void. Just know I left a little surprise on the inside of your pillow and if you have pink eye I have nothing to do with it. Moving on, I do think the wide receivers aren’t as bad as I originally projected. Flowers might finally have a breakout year and he was a phenomenal choice, the only problem is the Ravens are always run heavy. Run heavy? Yeah that's about right with the girls you bring home, those tortas for sure run HEAVY. All that to say his value is for sure capped. Don't let that first week fool you, he is going to come back to earth, but being the #1 WR in Baltimore that is still probably about 15 points a game. Higgins and Pickens are both the wide receiver twos on their own teams, and while they do get a higher volume than most other WR2s, I can’t fathom starting a guy who isn’t even the best player at his position on his own team. I guess it’s worked out so far, you've somehow managed to get one win. Then again, you were against Gabe, who only put up fifty-one points. That’s like taking candy from a baby, a big 6'4 baby with great hair, a great frame, and a really fat DIC....I digress.

I do really enjoy the bench though. Hubbard has had a really impressive start to the year, and while Rhamondre Stevenson has butterfingers, he still holds some value since New England is extremely stubborn with their running back situation (about the only thing he can hold). Even Worthy had a surprisingly good game this past week and could for sure be of value down the road. This team is definitely going to be volatile and prone to booms and a lot of busts. Then again, that’s nothing new for you, you're used to a lot of big fat busts in an empty, dark room, with the Balatro theme music playing in the background as you top out on ante 6 with a flush build.  Lots of Mahomo meant for this post, hopefully this team can get out there and motorboat some Tets (as in Tet McMillan, the WR for the Panthers) Hubba hubba. Good luck, big dog.
8. Fondle These Footballz (Brin)

We’re moving into the teams that are definitely getting better, and that are gonna make me eat my words as the season goes on. But at the same time, this team definitely has its flaws. Obviously you have the best player in the league, he finishes number one at his position almost every single year and guarantees you a minimum of ten points. Of course I’m talking about Brandon Aubrey. All jokes aside, you do probably have one of the best running back rooms in the league. CMC is a legit MVP candidate, as long as his ACL is okay, and DeAndre Swift has looked phenomenal on the Bears so far this year. I do fear his workload may be hindered a bit, because I think the backup, Kyle Monangai, might take a little work, but Swift is clearly the number one in that offense. Just better hope he stays getting the goal line work

You also have a really solid wide receiving group in both your starters Olave and Watson. The Packers wide receivers are always so hit or miss, but I think at this point Watson is solidified as the number one. Their running game has also been so bad they’d be better off with a Make-A-Wish kid in a wheelchair as their running back compared to whatever the fuck they got going on now, thus Sir Watson has been fed a lot and has been returning his value. Olave as well has garnered some of the most targets in the league so far this year. However, one has to ask how long that will last before homeboy inevitably takes a hit too big and confusedly starts stumbling around and throwing up gang signs because he doesn’t know where he is. Shockingly you have Brock Bowers on the bench and have yet to even see him play so that's yet another promising player for the future.

Somehow, against all offs, you’ve managed to start 2-0, with your brethren Justin Herbert at the helm. I don’t know how much longer you can start him with the way he’s playing, but it looks like Sam Darnold is back this week, so maybe he’ll get a chance to earn his stripes. Then again, who knows., Big Cock Lock has been absolutely balling. Is there some competition there? Is Sammy D a product of the system? Who cares, they’re winning, and so is your fantasy team. The more I look at this, the stronger I think this team actually is, but I gotta keep you humble and keep you in eighth place, because we can’t have a two-time champ before ninety percent of the league even gets a singular championship.
7. All My Opponents Goofy (Maggie)

This team is honestly pretty solid. I realize the majority of the league has a good enough wide receiving core to get my on a weekly basis, but very few people have two absolute studs at running back. Both Derrick Henry and James Cook are absolute workhorses, and they’ll put up anywhere from fifteen to thirty points a week. That alone separates you from the majority of the league. The problem I see though is the wide receivers. Garrett Wilson is a great addition, and New York is going to be losing a lot, so he’ll be getting more targets than a gentrifying neighborhood in Pittsburgh (fun fact, per Capita, Pittsburgh has the 2nd most targets in the world). Additionally, they finally got a gunslinger in Geno Smith who won't be thowing ducks and picks left and right. So while the Jets may be balls, at least he’ll be getting a good amount of fantasy points for mama.

My problem comes with the rest of them. Jameson Williams plays for one of the most explosive offenses, yet he’s an absolute dud. Maserati Marv was one of the highest touted prospects out of college, yet he also plays for one of the worst teams in the league and is dead weight. You’d expect the Cardinals to be throwing the ball a lot, and Jacoby Brisket is basically the Geno Smith of the NFC, but Marv has bricks for hands and has no idea how to get any separation from a defensive back. It's a true tragedy and I can't wait to try to trade for him in 2 weeks. While this is all a detriment to your team, there’s one saving grace....you have four fucking quarterbacks, and thank God you drafted four, because Jackson Dart is already out for the year and Caleb Williams pulled his left labia, so he’s gonna be missing a couple weeks. Now you just have to decide between Danny Dimes, who has yet to put up over twelve points, and Brock Purdy, who I personally don't like. He has never done me wrong or effected my life in any way, he just has a very punchable face. You know the kind, kinda like this one girl you may know. She has some buck teeth and a forehead the size of Texas, her name is something like Olive or Alive, I honestly can't remember, I think I curb stopped her the other week. My point is, fuck Brock Purdy, but you can't deny one thing, that boy has been putting up FAT fantasy points every single week.

We’re already approaching week three and the waiver wire is getting a bit bleak, but you definitely have some room to replace a few of these people, or offer a trade here and there, to strengthen your core where possible. I think this is going to be an extremely average team, and by average I mean slightly better than average. You should make the playoffs, but I don’t know that I see this as a championship roster as is. You’re my favorite autistic autodrafter, and I hope the three times you do change your lineup this whole year will be impactful enough to at least get a W over Brody. I think you’re unjustly 0-2, and hopefully your luck turns around here against Newpdogg. This is your rival week and boy is this rival weak. You better smack the shit out of her, because I got her ranked last, and I’m gonna look real stupid if you lose. Don’t let me down, big dog, Woof Woof, Alpha out!
6. Gay People Can't Play Football (Gabe)

I like this team, and I think it’s pretty solid. My worries come when you look at the second string of everyone. Sure, you have Ashton Jeanty, who’s looking like a stud with Klint Kubiak. Sure, you have Puka, who has yet to play a game, but we all know he’s good for a top five wide receiver season. Hell, you even have Mike Evans, who’s looking like the de facto number one in San Francisco because the substation has already eliminated half their team, Stribling, Pearsal, Demarcus Robinson, almost got Shanahan too, scary times being a niner fan, Mike Evans days are numbered. My point is, these are all great starters.

The problem comes when we look at Quinshon Judkins, who is on one of the worst, if not the worst, offenses in the league (Steelers are giving the Browns a run for their money this year). Homeboy has 50 yards in two games. You have Emeka Egbuka, who was expected to be the number one in Tampa, and he has eighty yards in two games. Then on the bench you have Terry McLaurin, who also was expected to be a number one wide receiver, and he just lost his starting QB and is gonna have to rely on Oregon legend Marcus Mariotta. Scarry Terry is not looking so scarry, he has sixty-four yards through two games. I think there’s a lot of potential for these guys to turn it around and have a better season, but right now it’s looking rough. That being said, the starters should consistently put up a solid seventy or eighty points, and then you just need the remaining players to have a somewhat decent week to sustain a W.

However, we see what happens when the starters don’t have a good week, and you drop a fat fifty burger, which is likely going to be the least amount of points scored this whole season by any one team. Lets just hope it's a fluke and it's good you got it out of your system early, but god damn, what a fucking shit show last week was. That’s gotta just be an anomaly where no one showed up and you kinda got burned because Puka didn’t play Monday Night after eveyone else on your lineup did, so I guess I can’t judge you too much, but I’m gonna pretend that was a Monday night mishap rather than you not switching your lineup. Because if that’s the case, you know I’m gonna have to come over there and beat your dick of! And if you do it again, I don’t know if I can take you myself, you clearly don't respect me so I’m gonna have to get another strong, burly, hunky, sexy man in Jordan to come over there too, and Jordan and I will both have to beat your dick off until you cum….to the realization that we’re not messing around, and this fantasy shit means something. Get it together, big dog and may the rest of your team turn out and stay healthy. I honestly don’t know where I’m gonna put you in future rankings. This team has me in a blender right now, I’m so conflicted whether this is a good team or a bad team, but only time will tell.
5. Baby got Dak (Jess)

Baby got Dak!!! Holy shit, girl, what a turnaround you’ve had in your few years of fantasy. I have you at five, but I think I might have to reconsider in the next set of rankings. The more I look at this team, the more I like it. You have two starting-caliber running backs, and while they may not be the greatest in the league, they’re both good enough to be better than the majority of everyone else’s starters. They’ll consistently get you a decent amount of points on a weekly basis, maybe they aren't dropping 20 bombs, but at least 10-12 is likely on Sundays. Jeremiyah Love has been through some hard falls because Arizona is ass, but at least they’re getting better. The Skattpack has also been really balling out, but in New York they do run a bit of a committee, and he just lost his best friend and CTE buddy in Jackson Dart. Not sure how this affects the Giants offense going forward, whether they run more through Cam or if they’re losing more games and have to pass the ball. But I guess we’ll see in the upcoming weeks. Could be good, could also tank his value.

Then on top of that, you have one of the best wide receiving cores in this entire league. Amon-Reezy Saint Breezy is obviously one of the best in the league, and extremely consistent. Davante Adams is gonna be hit or miss, and I think he only had a really good game last week because Puka was M.I.A, but when he returns, I expect Adams to lose a little value. That being said, he’s probably still a reasonable flex piece, or he could be traded for someone better. And if those two aren’t good enough, you have Rashee Rice, Matthew Golden, and Deebo Samuel all on your bench. The three of those guys are all gonna have themselves a surprisingly good year. Hell, you even have hometown hero, Denzel Boston, who has had an immaculate start to the season. I know he has a sexual predator throwing him the ball, but if he’s getting a touchdown every single week, who cares how many happy endings Deshaun Epstein got? The general depth across this team is PROBABLY the best in the league but I know the RB depth IS the best with Aaron Jones and even JCM or Alvin Kamara, who might not be great individually, but they could be packaged in a trade for better players down the road.

Maybe it’s The Life of a Showgirl, Maybe it’s their love story, and they deserve a happy ending (Not the Deshaun Watson kind). Maybe the Chiefs are just back, but Travis Kelce has looked like a Romeo to Taylors Juliet and he could be giving you top tight end value for the rest of the season. The more I look at this team, the more I like it, and I fear that this might be one of the top teams going into the next couple of rankings. I don’t know if I can handle you beating the shit out of me in this league and your family league. I’m gonna have to figure out some way to sabotage this, because I’m gonna be super butt hurt if you dick me down this year in not one but two leagues. Fuck, I’ve created a monster, I’m weirdly turned on, but also terrified. Is this hot that you’re good at fantasy football? Is this worrisome, that you’re better than me at my own game? I’m feeling very conflicted with all of my emotions and I’m gonna need some time to process this. I’d really appreciate if you would help me out and help me clear my head...and you know the one I’m talking about. Help me with that and you're number one in the power rankings every week.
4. Chrome Dome Clankers (Trevor)

I can hear it already "Man, you don’t deserve this", "Your team sucks", "Why are you ahead of me?", "You shouldn’t be top five". Stuff a sock in it, Daddy is home. I could’ve put myself top three, but I’m trying to be humble. I mean, realistically, I’m probably not top three right now, but post-draft, I thought I had a team of the gods and a real reason to be top three. The running backs terrify me, and I’m hoping that my woman beater, Josh Jacobs, comes back, because clearly he didn’t do anything wrong. I already got a handful of guys on IR, but at least I got Ja’Marr Chase and what could be the surprise QB of the year in New Orleans.

I’m gonna have to work some magic over the next couple of weeks until I get to week six, and hopefully have my totally innocent running back rejoin my team. That being said, the Packers have looked absolutely abysmal, and I don’t know how much of a difference him being on my team or not makes. But I guess we’ll have to wait and see. If any of y’all receive a trade offer that looks even remotely interesting and Josh Jacobs is attached, maybe you should take that. Just a thought. Totally nothing behind that. He’s for sure returning this year, and he’s definitely gonna be a top ten running back when he does. Hit me up, gangbangers.
3. LaPorta Potty Party (Max)

Welcome back to my yearly ritual of glazing you and your team. However, I think this is the first year in four years that it seems I don’t have you in first place post-draft. Do I still like this team? Absolutely. But should they be number one? Unlikely. Especially now that we’re a few weeks into the season, I’m realizing that this team is good, but definitely not number one. Sure, you have probably the best running back combination in the league, and the three-headed monster of Lamar, Gibbs, and Walker. Yes, Lamar is still a running back, but damn, he’s even been doing a bad job of that recently. Bring back Zay Flowers so he can actually get some fantasy points. Realistically, Bucky is a great third option for the three headed monter you got brewing.

Unfortunately, it seems your wide receivers have all suffered some sort of injury. Nico Collins already has a hamstring something or other, Alec Pierce never fully recovered from his ankle injury or whatever it was, Keenan Allen has a DUI, DK Metcalf… I have nothing nice to say about DK Metcalf, so imma do what my mom always taught me and if I have nothing nice to say, absolutely let em' have it! Fuck DK Metcalf, bricks for hands mf, learn how to catch a ball. I saw a stat that he has more drops than he does catches this year. Can you believe that??? Probably because he has been so ass but in reality I just made that stat up. But the fact that you believed that even for a second says volumes about this guy so far this year. He’s on my shit list, and I’m sure you’re sick of him too. But this whole teams wide receiver situation is U-G-L-Y, you ain’t got no alibi, it’s butt ugly. I do really like the addition of Isaiah Likely. While he only scored four or five points last week, he had ten targets, which is better than most wide receivers in this league. Then obviously, to top it all off, you have the GOAT, Chris Boswell. However, he too is on my shit list for missing a couple kicks so far this year. I think the problem is the Steelers are just on my shit list, and anyone Steeler-related in fantasy is pissing me off except for our glorious King Jaylen Warren who can do no wrong.

Sorry to disappoint this year. I know you probably already had the lube and tissues in hand, ready to have a stroke to this team, but this isn’t the year. For the first time in Seattle Seacock history, I’m going to glaze you like Riley Reid on the Blacked couch. Maybe if some of these receivers get healthy again and DK learns how to catch a ball, you might stay top three, but right now I fear that in the next rankings you may be just a bit lower than 5.
2. Like a Good Naber (Katie)

It is a tragedy what your team is doing to you right now. As you can see, I have you as my second best team, yet you are 0-2 through the first two weeks of this regular season. Does your team suck? Did I make a mistake ranking you second? Perhaps, but I’d like to think that I am all-knowing and ball-knowing, and this is just a case of bad luck. In one of my other money leagues, I had a pick around the turn as well, and it was my wet dream to get Chase Brown and Omarion Hampton. I ended up with Chase Brown, but Hampton was gone when it got back to me, and I ended up with Josh Jacobs instead, and we all know how that turned out. I think that was a phenomenal one-two pick. And then to turn around and get both Tetairoa McMillan and Malik Nabers at the 3/4 turn, this was a masterclass of a draft. Hell, you even got Colston Loveland at the 5th, who was one of the top tight ends last year and was extremely promising going into this year.

But I guess we can’t all live in a candy land, and we have to face the realities of the NFL and fantasy football. Drake Maye, who was the MVP runner-up last year, takes a shit in his pants every single time he drops back to throw a pass. Omarion Hampton is great, but he is on a team whose offensive line is about as impenetrable as a piece of Swiss cheese. Malik Nabers is one of the best wide receivers in the league, but his quarterback just busted his knee and is out for the rest of the season, and he’s gonna have to rely on, "Fuck it, Malik’s down there somewhere" Jameis Winston. Tet McMillan too has been out-targeted by the second stringer, Jalen Coker. Is Tet washed or is Carolina just pivoting for the first couple weeks? I guess only time will tell. And to top it all off, your fifth round pick in Colston Loveland has one catch for three yards through two weeks. This guy was supposed to be the next Antonio Gates, the next Tony Gonzalez, the next Gronkowski, yet here he is looking like The Big Lebowski.

So while you are 0-2, I do believe this team can turn it around with a little bit of luck. Please, please, please turn this around these next couple weeks so I don’t look like a complete moron for having you top tier only to be 0-4 when the next set of rankings comes out. Please, Katie, I’m dying. The group is gonna clown me if I have a team that is 0-4 at the quarter way mark ranked as my second overall. Please, Katie, please!!!!! Fuck Brin up this week.
1. Bootyhole Browns (Brody)

Alas, the time has come to talk about number one. Now, don’t get it twisted, this was post-draft and I believed this was the best team by quite a large margin. I’m not so sure that margin is still as large today after a few weeks but you still have a top tier team. Sure, you have Bijan, who is about the only coherent piece of the Atlanta offense, and Penix being back definitely helped, but through those first three weeks he was about the only one who could get more than ten yards in Atlanta. Does that change with Penix back? Does this reduce his role a little? Thursday night football says no, but they were also playing the packers who are gonna be lucky to get 5 wins this seasons with the way they are playing.  Javonte has been underwhelming, but he plays for an extremely high-powered offense, so he should fall into a touchdown every other week.

Then I looked at the WR room and thought with DJ Moore, Rome Odunze, Carnell Tate, and BTJ, this was going to be the God Squad, the'ye all gonna absolutely ball out this year. Unfortunately, it seems those expectations have been curbed and they have all been extremely underwhelming so far, to where you have to start Dontayvion Wicks. Sure, he’s not a bad start, but I’m sure that’s not someone you thought would be on your team, let alone starting in week three. Obviously, you have basically a top-tier wide receiver one in Trey McBride, so realistically, if your second wide receiver only puts up seven points, that’s basically a regular tight end week, so it cancels out. I think the biggest weak point right now is the quarterback. I truly thought Jayden Daniels was gonna be a top three quarterback this year, and he still has the potential for that, but that boy has the bones of the Con Man from SpongeBob aka his more formal name, Glass bones guy. But at least you got Kyler in the meantime, who also is a bit injury prone, and if we’re being honest, Carson Wentz looked better than Kyler, so realistically, is this job even his?

Not sure where I’ll end up with this team in future weeks, but it’s for sure still one of the better teams, and it has a lot of potential still to go. Pretty much your whole bench is a bunch of guys who could be top 15 at their position if they stay healthy and are utilized properly. It’s a damn shame I gotta put you at first, because Maggie is always glazing you about how you know ball, and I unfortunately have to succumb and agree on this one occasion. Don’t get too comfy up there. This is the post-draft rankings, so in a couple weeks you might see a bit of a slide and have to have a bit of a reality check. But in the meantime, enjoy the throne King.

posts.title: 2026 Weeks 1-5 Rankings
posts.hubLabel:
The First Trimester
(Of your fantasy baby)
blocks:
Five weeks in. This is the 30% check-in, the first trimester of your fantasy baby, and the ultrasound looks rough. We have one undefeated team, and by some miracle of God every squad has at least one win. That's a shot at me. I'm second to last, out here acting like the new Matte. I can't judge Olivia for being last. She has a special condition, so this is more so embarrassing for me, the reigning champion, than anyone else

My preseason prediction had the Chargers running the AFC West, however, Herbert and that allegedly loaded roster with a "great new coaching staff" is 0-5. Eighty-four points scored, 129 allowed, zero wins. Kicking that back to our league, that's our girl Katie. I had Like a Good Naber second in my preseason power rankings, Hampton and Nabers at the turn, MVP runner up at the helm, I wrote that post like the trophy was on her counter. Only fitting that the team with Omarion Hampton, possibly the biggest disappointment (aside for Gabe coming out the closet) is sitting at 2-3 and is now (spoiler alert) tenth in this weeks rankings. On the flip side of the coin, you have Minnesota who was the team every analyst skipped over in August. The Vikings are somehow 5-0 and looking to continue that dominance as they have a handful of easy games up until week 9 when they hit a few roadbumps before it's smooth sailing the rest of the way . They have scored 109 points while only allowing 64. To but that in the Seattle Seacocks lens, that's Max. I had LaPorta Potty Party third after the draft and I told him not just one, but two teams were coming out of the draft ahead of him. I guess he took that personally as he is now 5-0 and securely in first.

It's been a rough start to my season and the same can be said for a handful of you, so what's the remedy? Waiver Wire moves? Trades? Who can say, but all I know is something needs to change. So, will some moves be made? Probably. I am more than willing to make a trade, but be on the lookout. We have a shark in the water committing nefarious acts of treason and trade. Miss Herbert (not soon to be Madison Beer) has been hustling and making moves on innocent unsuspecting bystanders. I can't hate the player because in the wise words of someone, "that's how they learn", so instead, I have to hate the game, because half of y'all aren't setting lineups, let alone willing to talk turkey. I don't know if y'all ain't never tasted glory before, but there is a share of a few hundred dollars up for grabs. In this economy, Donald Trump's America, that could buy you like half a tank of gas and a Big Mac. Sheesh, maybe I'm the only broke one who is looking for a few extra dollars in my bank account. Surely that can't be the case, let's take a look at everyone's situation and see how luxurious all y'all are living and why none of you are jumping at the chance for a few hundred bones.

Maggie and Brody moved to SF (probably both working for Sam Altman at this point) and are living in a 1 BR, 1/2 BR apartment with a dog for about 8k a month...must be nice. Max and Katie ended up moving in together with two dogs, living that D.I.N.K. lifestyle (Double income no kids for those of you who don't keep up with the youngin slang). Gabe is in the heart of downtown Seattle with a great view of all the night time shootings and stabbings. Jordan, Olivia, and Haley all got places with waterfront views (Great or not, you can still somewhat see the water). Brendan gets zero bitches and lives in Shoreline, so all he does is work, crank hog, and stack his bread. Then you got Jess and I living in fucking Puyallup with her brother and parents, wooptee fucking doo doo.

I get why Brin is the only one hustling out here. She's unemployed, exploring Europe, and living her best life. Shit I guess the red light district is getting a little expensive though, so a few hundred dollars could go a long way for her. From that angle I understand why this league is dryer than a woman's panties when Brendan tells them he is gonna rip 200mg of a cannabis cocktails and then have himself a Dragon Ball Z marathon.

I'm only here to make fun of you all and stimulate the fantasy football economy because we are in a RECESSION! Enough bashing everyone though, I'll save the rest of that for your specific writeups. Without further ado, here's what we got through the first five weeks of football, and how I think things have changed up in this league.

12. Blowin' My J's (Jordan)
Change: -1
Record: 2-3

Hey bud, what's going on here? This team has been a shit show since day one. I like the all-J draft idea, but the problem is that all went out the window when you let Brin absolutely violate you. She walked in, took two of your best, and left you a bag of chips and a slap on the ass. If that's your thing no judgment, I just thought it would be from Gabe or I not a WOMAN!?!?!

The ONE and ONLY positive about this team is you do have the best player in the league in Josh Allen. The rest of this team is not only dick, but it is balls too. Jaylen Warren has been balling out, but Rico Dowdle is supposed to be back this week, and who knows what Warren is good for once that happens. Justice Hill is a pathetic excuse for an RB2. Find someone on the waivers or try to trade, because the two Brin gave you are probably worse than Hill, which again is a violation to your dignity.

I honestly can't hate the wide receivers. Jaylen Waddle is a good player, but he plays for the Broncos, and their offense has been extremely underwhelming. Luther Burden is solid, but under the terrorist Tyson Bagent, he is useless. Fortunately Caleb returns this week from his left labia injury (hopefully). It sure would be nice if you still had a receiver on an undefeated team, possibly a guy who is arguably top five, I wonder where you could find one of those....

There isn't much else to talk about. Your whole bench is on injured reserve so unless you plan on waiting until week 10 to make a playoff push, I am not seeing the vision. I love the commitment to the J's, but Brin tainted it, and at this point you should sell out and try to win at least a few games. You're lucky we didn't suggest a punishment this year or else you would be the front-runner, hell we still might. If you care, which is a big if, my suggestion would be to talk to your father. He seems to be a football know-it-all and a fantasy expert as well, and he might have a suggestion for who to pick up and who to drop.

Greedily, my suggestion is to trade Josh Allen for an absolute haul. I would love to be your suitor, but I don't know that I can offer everything you're looking for. Good luck out there, kiddo. My last bit of advice is next time Brin tries to trade with you, tell her to at least bring some lube.

11. Newpdogg (Olivia)
Change: +1
Record: 1-4

Whoop whoop, big dog, moving up in the world! Last week 12th, this week 11th, next week 10th. Shiiiiiit you'll be first in no time. Granted, the guy you climbed over is Jordan, and he just traded away his best players while his bench is littered with guys on injured reserve, but that's neither here nor there, we're here to talk about you and boy, do I got some words to type.

At this point, hand the sticks over to Uncle Jimmy. If you want, I'll add him as a ghost manager who is not such a "ghost" manager again. I think the whole league is laughing at you and it has nothing to do with your fantasy football skills. In reality, I honestly don't hate this team, you've just gotten unlucky, between the injuries and the fact that the Eagles are absolute dog shit. I thought it was a federal crime to kill a bald eagle. If that's the case, the FBI is on the way to your house right now. I have no doubt that you drafting the whole Eagles offense is the reason they are underperforming. Sure, Jalen Hurts was never a good quarterback, just a tush-push merchant who gets off to get a bunch of dudes to push his bootyhole. But I thought with A.J. Brown gone, DeVonta Smith was gonna have himself a great year. Dallas Goedert is somehow always a top-five or top-ten tight end. Saquon Barkley is an absolute freak of nature, and you, Oliver Newport Cigarettes (might need to workshop that one), cursed him with your atrocious, horrible, no good, very bad juju.

To bring it back to a positive note, this team could turn it around later in the year, but it needs to happen pretty dang soon. Henderson and Lloyd are good for maybe a combined ten points. Sutton and Downs, or Diggs when he's healthy, are good for a combined fifteen to twenty, max. Your first-round pick, Sir Cedarian DeLeon Lamb, has been balling out and is the only thing keeping this team afloat. You need some luck, or some help from Uncle Chuck, because right now, it is looking bleak.

Your one win did come against the worst team in the league, but you did put up 130 that week so maybe there is hope, just ignore every other week where you've been averaging about 75. To no ones surprise, you have the lowest points scored in the league, so to reiterate for the 6th time, you need to make some changes. Maybe it is just me, but I would go out on a limb and say you have checked this app maybe once a week and you don't particularly give a shit so I'm just yapping. I know you're just along for the ride and the comradery that comes with it, but it would be nice to see you kick some ass here and there. I really just wanna see you beat down on Brody and Maggie, since I can't, and I gotta send in the big guns. Turn off Jersey Shore and turn on some ESPN every once in a while, get a grip on this team, and spin the block on your opps.

10. Like a Good Naber (Katie)
Change: -8
Record: 2-3

Listen, I know I had you at second in the last rankings, and this is quite the drop to tenth. I do realize that you have been on a two-game winning streak after starting 0-3, so maybe there is hope to climb the rankings by the next trimester. In reality, I don't particularly hate this team and I think the more I look at it, I can convince myself that it's pretty solid and I had you second for a reason. It has just been disappointing through these first five weeks. Will things change? Maybe. But those first few weeks, I was terrified for this team and maybe that is what is swaying this decision to drop you down towards the bottom.

You have two of the hypothetical best running backs in the league in Chase Brown and Omarion Hampton. I was extremely high on both of these guys and would have loved to draft them. However, they have been anything but good, and Hampton has been more disappointing than probably anyone in fantasy. Hampton's production for the Chargers has been a bigger disappointment than when Teddy sees a rabbit on the TV, only for it to run off, and now she gotta sit through nothing but gambling and beer commercials with no animals in them, the disappointment is immeasurable. Brown too has been decent, but the Bengals, for whatever reason, have not been giving him touchdowns. I get it, they're a pass-first team, but I really thought Chase Brown would be catching a few more balls and stumbling into the endzone more than just once this year so far. In that same vein, Woody Marks as a running back is not great, and he is the backup at this point. Maybe this week, with David Montgomery injured, he can show a little gusto and get a few points, but I wouldn't count on it.

Your wide receivers are close to extraordinary, but they have been up and down. I think Nabers is one of the best in the league, and he proved that last week, but I wouldn't expect him to get 20 targets every single week. Maybe it was a blessing that Jameis took over, because that boy slings the rock. I still have some caution with Nabers but he is a must start so nothing you can do but sit back and enjoy the ride. Same goes for McMillan, he had a great week the last time he played, but that was with Jalen Coker sidelined and against the worst defense in the league. So can we really hold a candle to that week and believe this is what he is now? In theory I really like these guys, it is hard to truly get behind them and put your whole hearted trust in them every week. Not that you have too much of a choice but it do be a bit worrisome

The depth is there with Germie Bernard. I think that's a great pickup, and I'm very angry that you got him and I didn't, because for at least the next three or four weeks he should be one of Aaron Rodgers' top targets in that pass-heavy offense. Even Keon Coleman, though he's not very reliable, is a good start every once in a while. Across the board, I think you have pretty decent depth. That depth keeps going with Wan'Dale Robinson, Devaughn Vele, and Colston Loveland. All good adds, and while none of them have really proven they are long-term options, Loveland is about the only one who could be consistent, and even that is hard to say, because the Bears have been missing their quarterback for the past few weeks (He pulled his left labia but should be back this week).

You did have a super sneaky waiver wire add that I do really fuck with and that is our glorious king Tyreek Hill. Will he return? Who knows. Will he even be the same guy if he does? Who knows. BUT IF HE DOES COME BACK, especially to the Chiefs, a team that needs a wide receiver badly right now, he still has that chemistry with Mahomes, and he could get back to the version of himself that was chasing the single-season receiving record, but alas, Only time will tell.

Things are turning around for you and this team, with wins in your last two. It's an in-house matchup this week, and you got Max. Please be the first one to give this boy an L. You two should put something on the line, like loser has to take the dogs on all the walks next week or maybe something crazier like the loser has to sign up for the Taiwanese Army, get drafted when they inevitably go to war with China, go to war and help overthrow the Chinese government, then live in Beijing for 5 years, give intel to the US about expanding data centers and their AI plans to take over the world, sneak into Arisaka tower and fight the ghost of Mao Zedong to save the US and world. Idk, just something light like that as a suggestion, but you do you.

9. Gay People Can't Play Football (Gabe)
Change: -3
Record: 3-2

Yeah, yeah, yeah. I know you're 3-2 and you have a winning record, but you're still ninth in my eyes. This is a good team, and it seems like things are trending the right way, but for some reason I like all the other teams just a bit more. You're second to Jordan in the injured reserve squad, three guys, all pretty irrelevant, and Baker is hurt. The rest of this team is probably better than it has been producing which is what leads you to ninth but there is plenty of season left for you to rise back up.

When I go through my process of rankings, I compare teams next to each other in a split screen window so I can see how your RBs/WRs/Bench all line up, and you having Puka in your flex really throws the whole thing off. Sure he has been injured and playing monday nights so he has been either a last minute add or remvoe so the flex makes snese, but I'll see somebody with CeeDee Lamb or Ja'Marr Chase in a starter spot, then I'll look at Emeka Egbuka and Mike Evans and think, oh my god, yeah, your team sucks compared to them. Then I realize Puka is sitting in your flex and everything I just thought is null and void.

Despite the shade I just threw to Egbuka and Evans, the wide receivers are your strong point. Puka, Mike Evans, God willing he stays healthy, and Terry McLaurin are all bona fide number ones on their teams. They should get anywhere from five to ten targets a game, and in Puka's case, twenty. Emeka Egbuka and Romeo Doubs aren't always going to be your starters, but as backups they are pretty decent. Egbuka is allegedly the number one over there, but the Bucs have been trash these past couple weeks, so I don't have a lot of faith in starting him. Doubs has hit his peak, since A.J. Brown is supposed to be back soon and he'll be back to 5 points a game if he is lucky. Kind of disappointing that in the game Drake Maye dropped a 40-bomb, Romeo Doubs had one catch. Not sure how that makes any sense, but he's inconsistent, to say the least.

The biggest scrubs so far have been running backs, and I'm not sure where you even go from here. The waiver wire is already thin. Ashton Jeanty is an automatic start every single week despite his struggles with getting into the endzone. I feel like you have to start Judkins too, but he has been piss poor on a Browns offense that has somehow been mediocre. He's dealing with an ankle issue, so who knows what the next few weeks look like, whether he's full speed or they're easing him in and keeping him off the field on limited touches. I would tell you to use Kenny Gainwell or R.J. Harvey, but those two are probably the worst players on your team. Which is saying a lot, seeing that you have Tank Dell, who last time we saw him on a football field, stepped on a landmine planted by an IDF soldier and blew his knee back to Palestine.

Granted, who am I to talk? This is clearly the winning solution. You've only made one move so far this year, and I believe that was picking up Tank Dell off waivers. Maybe the action of inaction is working in your favor. You got three wins and I only have one, so I gotta get off my high and mighty horse about how I know ball, when the only balls I know is yours in the back of my throat.

8. Chrome Dome Clankers (Trevor)
Change: -4
Record: 1-4

Bruh, I don't know what is going on here. I thought I had myself a top-five team, and maybe I still do, but boy have I been unlucky. At least that's the excuse I'm telling myself.

I have a top-tier running back in Kyren Williams, and Ja'Marr Chase as one of the best wide receivers in the league. Josh Jacobs already pleaded no contest on the battery charge and he's still stuck on the commissioner's exempt list, so that backfield is just Kyren until the league says hitting women is acceptable. A.J. Brown got stuck on IR, but he practiced today, so the whole out-for-the-month thing might already be dead. I did get a solid pickup in Ollie Gordon, and I have arguably one of the best tight ends in Tyler Warren, but the rest of this team has been lackluster, to say the least. Which makes sense, they're supposed to be by bench scrubs who are not meant to be starting on a weekly basis

I'm sticking with unlucky as my excuse. I have the most points scored against me, and it isn't even close. I'm about fifty points clear of everybody else. Olivia is the only one anywhere near me, and she has been pretty unlucky too, just shy of 600 points against on the season, that's about 120 points a week. Take her out and the next closest is about a hundred points back, so every week I've had to score about twenty more points than everyone else just to stay afloat and get a win. Sure I may have the third-lowest points scored, ahead of only Olivia and Katie, but that is neither here nor there, it's totally the points against!

I'm hoping I can get a win on Jordan this week, seeing that Brin ravaged his team, but I'm not all that hopeful. Wish me luck out there. If the commissioner doesn't get to three wins, another edition of this isn't coming out. Count your blessings, and start playing your bench players against me if you want me to keep making fun of y'all.

7. Baby Choda (Brendan)
Change: +2
Record: 2-3

Low-kirk-enuinely, this team is kinda kicking ass. I don't have a whole lot of faith in all of these players, so I still have you a bit lower, but if they keep producing the rest of the season, I won't have a choice but to move you up.

Mahomes is one of the best in the league, and coming off this ACL he looks like a new man, back in MVP form. Your running backs, Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard, have both been pretty exceptional. Max still has the best backfield in the league but you're giving him a run for his money in second. And you are not actually giving him a run for his money at all, it is pretty clear his team is way better, he has the number one and the number two. Taylor has been a bit underwhelming, yet he's still the sixth overall running back. Hubbard too has consistently been putting up great numbers for an 8th round pick or whatever he was, so honestly still pretty good for a guy with autism.

I do worry about the wide receivers. Pickens is a great receiver, and while the Ravens are not a pass-first team, Flowers is about the only relevant pass catcher there, and if he keeps producing, game recognize game. The problem with Pickens is he stays the Cowboys' number two behind CeeDee Lamb. He may not put up a bunch of points every week, but George Pickens will catch about any ball thrown his way, kinda like your throat goat girl with the herpes. Shit, she would put up a good fight with him. If they went ball for ball, I think she might win and catch more balls than him. I digress, my point was, he's on a pass-first offense, but he's still the number two behind CeeDee Lamb which can be annoying for your fantasy escapades. Even the bench has some pretty decent options too. Tee Higgins has been producing on that Bengals air raid offense, Xavier Worthy and Kenyon Sadiq haven't been exceptional, but they have a chance to matter. Kansas City is desperate for a wide receiver, and Sadiq is still a rookie growing into his role.

Aside form just the players and their  issues, you have the second most points scored, which honestly shocked me. I didn't realize this team was balling like that. I thought you were a Josh Allen merchant, and if you didn't have him, you were nothing. Clearly I see the new solution. The way to win these leagues is two defenses, two kickers, and keeping a guy on IR who has no chance of returning this season, I guess he's just the vibes and glue guy who keeps the team together mentally and emotionally. This is still a pretty good team, and the only reason you're in the middle of the pack is because I'm skeptical they keep playing like this. You did daddy dick me, though, so prove me wrong again and keep climbing king.

6. Bootyhole Browns (Brody)
Change: -5
Record: 4-1

All right, now we got Brody's Bitchin' Bootyhole Browns, and this boy is busy being busted, because this is the lowest ranked 4-1 team in the league. How the hell do you have four wins and can't even crack the top five? Crazy, you should speak to the selection committee about that one. You do have some pretty good players on this team, but the reason I have you down this low is the lack of consistency thus far.

Obviously you have one of the best running backs in the league in Bijan, who's basically a cheat code for an easy twenty to thirty points. It's a damn shame Michael Penix had to come back, because when he was out or when they let Tua's 6 brain cells run that offense, the show had to run through Bijan. Javonte Williams certainly not a great RB in terms of skill but he is a merchant of being on a good team. Maybe he's not the most efficient running back, but the Cowboys will be in the red zone enough that he'll fall into a touchdown or two almost every week.

To no ones surprise, the inconsistency is at wide receiver. Sure, you have a pseudo wide receiver one in Trey McBride, because he puts up numbers like he's the number one option on a team, but the problems arise with the other two. As we approach scary season and the end of October, Carnell Tate and DJ Moore are more than a little spooky. DJ Moore has missed a couple games now and left a few with that dang shoulder issue. He did have that phenomenal week one, but it was really only on the back of five catches, so how reliable is that going forward? When he is back and healthy will he be able to go 5 for 100 and a TD? Or on that rush first, Josh Allen improvisation ass team, will he be lucky to get 5 catches for 50 yards? Time shall tell I guess. While Carnell Tate is clearly the number one option in Tennessee, Tennessee is whack and winless. You'd think they'd be throwing the ball a ton and he would be eating since they always seem to be losing, but so far he hasn't been all that exceptional. Maybe down the stretch he turns on the burners like most rookie wide receivers do and catches fire to help you secure your first chip. But through the first five weeks, it is looking rough and you might want to start leaning on any of those other guys.

Thank God you got a bench of "studs" or at least that's how you can sell them to half the league who don't keep up with football. BTJ is only really worth holding because he's on the trading block. The Jags have all but forgotten who he was his rookie year, and his only path to mattering seems to lay in the balance of getting traded to some wide-receiver-needy team before the deadline. The problem is the teams in that conversation are the Steelers, the Colts, or perhaps the Chiefs, to name a few, and those are not exactly the perfect fit for a guy you're hoping can put up ten points a game (except the Chiefs which would be a homerun, but they'll bring back Tyreek before they trade a draft pick I would imagine). I am shocked to see Rome Odunze sitting there, but in all fairness, he has been a bit of a bust. He runs the most routes and has the most snaps of all Bears WRs, but for whatever reason he is just not seeing production. Probably doesn't help he has been catching balls from Bagnet and Keenum the past 2 weeks while his starter has been out due to Ovarian pain. The one hope for this bench would be KC Concepcion who has looked great, but unfortunately is potentially hurt now. Not to mention, Denzel Boston has low-key been the breadwinner so far (at least in terms of TDs). Still a toss-up though for who will actually emerge or if they will both be decent options for the Predator to throw to. As the season goes on, we'll see how that changes I guess.

Across the board, though, this team is pretty solid, and you have a good foundation, as long as some of these guys can keep growing into their roles. Charbonnet is a sneaky sleeper because the Seahawks' run game has been atrocious, and while he was no savior, last year, he was the king of the goal line. If he comes back, that's a huge addition. The only thing you gotta worry about is if Jayden Daniels can keep that chicken wang in check. He already snapped it once so he better slap a brace on the elbow. That thing is still asking to get snapped every time he runs the ball or takes a hit, Drink some more milk dude!

Do I feel bad you're in the middle of the pack? No. I could for sure see this team climbing over the next couple weeks. But until DJ Moore and Carnell Tate start to consistently prove themselves, or Odunze or Concepcion take that next step, you're not on the big hitters list yet.

5. Baby got Dak (Jess)
Change: -
Record: 3-2

I look at this team and I realize maybe I should have put you slightly higher, but the damage is done. You're sitting at five. I'll give you the breakdown, but I'm probably gonna end up glazing this team more than I've glazed you the past couple weeks. Which really isn't all that much, because I've been sick, and you refuse to touch me when I'm patient zero.

We'll start by talking trash, because this team is struggling at running back. Jeremiyah Love and Cam Skattebo are both great running backs. The problem is their teams aren't using them the way they should. Skattebo gets a good amount of carries, but the Giants are very seldom in the red zone, so he isn't feasting off that. Last game, when they were in the red zone, they handed it to Najee Harris, which is an unbelievable choice. Not sure if they're just trying to preserve the Skattpack for the rest of the season, because God knows he could run through a wall, and he should be getting all the goal line touches. Love is a phenomenal running back too. One of the most talented guys to come out of college, raw talent and the projections to match. The problem is he's on the Cardinals. They've been surprisingly decent, but they don't run the ball. They're a pass-first team, and they seem to be limiting his carries. He was hurt at the beginning of the year, and since he's come back they've been mixing in Tyler Allgeier. You also have to be on the lookout, because James Conner is coming off IR in the next couple of games. Do I think he's going to have an impact? Very unlikely. This running back core has been sketchy, to say the least. I'm shocked you haven't started Aaron Jones, because while Jordan Mason has been out, Aaron Jones has sneakily been one of the best running backs in the league for where you drafted him and what he's given back.

Okay, haterade's done. Time to talk about the strongest part of this team, which is the wide receivers. Most teams have one, maybe two good wide receivers they can start every week. The elite teams have three they can safely start. You have four and a half, five, maybe even six that I would feel confident starting every single week. It's ridiculous. The best are Rashee Rice and Amon-Ra. Rice has been up and down, but he's a no-brainer, because the Chiefs are only getting more injured every single week. Matthew Golden has taken an unbelievable step here in his second year and is looking like a league winner from where you picked him up. It's a shame Deebo has gotten hurt, but San Francisco has wide receivers dropping left and right, so his usage was through the roof for the first few games while the substation keeps taking its toll. I'm not in love with Davante Adams or Denzel Boston, but they're both solid flex pieces if you need them. If I'm you, I'm trying to trade away one or two of those guys, or pair one with a running back, to get a better running back and raise this team's ceiling.

4. All My Opponents Goofy (Maggie)
Change: +3
Record: 1-4

3. Jockstraps (Haley)
Change: +7
Record: 2-3

2. Fondle These Footballz (Brin)
Change: +6
Record: 4-1

1. LaPorta Potty Party (Max)
Change: +2
Record: 5-0
